---
title: "simstim config check"
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Find mistakes in the config files, each with its file and line.

```text
simstim config check [flags]
```

Reads config.toml and hosts.toml, and prints each mistake on one line, as file:line: message. It finds TOML errors, unknown keys, and values of the wrong type or outside their list. It checks legacy secret commands and structured definitions with the same rules as a session start. It also finds two spellings of one key and machines without a provider or an id. It also finds keys, sizes and times that do not parse, and hosts without a usable name or ssh. For an unknown key, it names the nearest known key. It exits with 1 when it finds an error, and with 0 when it finds only warnings, or nothing. With `--json`, it prints the report as one object, with the same exit codes.

## Examples

```sh
simstim config check
simstim config check --json
```

## Flags

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON for scripts, and ask nothing (see docs/how-to/scripting.md) |

## Flags from the parent command

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--debug[=<categories>]` | turn on the debug mode, with every category, or with the categories listed: attach, net, memory, launcher, runtime. A list binds only in the = form, such as `--debug=net` |
| `--debug-file <file>` | write the client's debug records to this file. On its own, it turns on every category (SIMSTIM_DEBUG_FILE does the same) |
| `--no-color` | print no colour (NO_COLOR does the same) |
| `--no-input` | ask nothing: a question that needs an answer fails with exit code 4, and names the flag that answers it (SIMSTIM_NO_INPUT=1 does the same) |

Part of [`config`](config.md): show the configuration.
